title: Problem Documentation and Imports
content: The header documents Erdős Problem #98 on distinct distances for points in general position ($\text{no 3 collinear} \wedge \text{no 4 concyclic}$). The question is whether $h(n)/n \to \infty$, where $h(n)$ is the minimum distinct distances over all $n$-point general-position configurations. Even $h(n) \ge n$ is unknown. Upper bounds: Pach ($n^{\log_2 3}$) and EFP ($n \cdot e^{c\sqrt{\log n}}$). Imports Mathlib's inner product spaces, special functions (log, exp, sqrt), Finset, and filters.

title: General Position: No 3 Collinear, No 4 Concyclic
content: `PointConfig n` maps $\text{Fin } n \to \text{EuclideanSpace } \mathbb{R} \; (\text{Fin } 2)$. `NoThreeCollinear P` forbids any three distinct points lying on a common affine line, checked via the vanishing of $ax + by + c$ at all three. `NoFourConcyclic P` forbids any four distinct points lying on a common circle, checked via equal distances to a center. `InGeneralPosition P` requires injectivity plus both conditions. These constraints eliminate structured configurations like integer lattices ($\sqrt{n} \times \sqrt{n}$) that achieve the minimum in the unrestricted problem.

title: Distinct Distances and the Function $h(n)$
content: `numDistinctDistances P` counts the distinct *positive* pairwise distances in the configuration: $|\{\|P_i - P_j\| : i,j \in [n], \|P_i - P_j\| > 0\}|$. This is computed by imaging all pairs into $\mathbb{R}$, filtering positive values, then taking the cardinality. `h n` $= \inf\{\text{numDistinctDistances}(P) : P \in \text{GenPos}(n)\}$ via `sInf`. The function $h$ is the central object: Erdős conjectures $h(n)/n \to \infty$ but even $h(n) \ge n$ is open.

title: Pach's Upper Bound: $h(n) < n^{\log_2 3}$
content: Axiomatizes Pach's construction: there exist general-position configurations with fewer than $n^{\log_2 3} \approx n^{1.585}$ distinct distances, eventually for all large $n$. The construction uses recursive Horton-type sets. The exponent $\log_2 3$ arises from a divide-and-conquer: split $n$ points into 3 groups of $n/2$, recursing on the distances. This is stated via `Filter.atTop` (eventually for all $n$).

title: Erdős-Füredi-Pach Bound: $h(n) < n \cdot e^{c\sqrt{\log n}}$
content: The best known upper bound: there exist general-position configurations with fewer than $n \cdot \exp(c\sqrt{\log n})$ distinct distances for some constant $c > 0$. This is much closer to linear than Pach's $n^{1.585}$, showing that $h(n)$ grows at most slightly superlinearly. Formalized using `Real.exp` and `Real.sqrt` composed with `Real.log`. The construction refines Pach's method using more sophisticated point placements.
mathContext: $\exists c > 0: h(n) < n \cdot e^{c\sqrt{\log n}}$ eventually; note $n \cdot e^{c\sqrt{\log n}} = o(n^{1+\varepsilon})$ for all $\varepsilon > 0$

title: The Erdős Conjecture: $h(n)/n \to \infty$
content: `ErdosProblem98` axiomatizes the main conjecture: $h(n)/n \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$, formalized as `Filter.Tendsto (fun n => h(n)/n) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop`. This says that general-position constraints force superlinearly many distinct distances. The conjecture is remarkably strong given the EFP bound: $h(n)$ must grow faster than $n$ but slower than $n \cdot e^{c\sqrt{\log n}}$, leaving a very narrow window.
